text:
Sophia: Hi team — our Private VPC deployment started failing outbound calls to Redwood hosted models after a network change. App servers behind corporate egress proxy get TLS handshake errors (logs show "tls: unknown certificate authority"), but from my laptop (on same corp network) curl works. Can you help triage? :confused:

Jordan: Sorry you're hitting this. Quick questions: did anything change on the proxy (MITM/TLS inspect) or firewall/egress allowlist around the same time? Also can you paste a short repro (curl) and the exact error from app logs?

Sophia: Ops team rolled an update to the proxy cluster around 05:10 UTC to enable SNI-based routing + upgraded the MITM cert. We suspect the new CA isn't trusted by the app image. App log (snippet):
```
2025-11-02T05:17:22Z ERROR outbound: tls handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2025-11-02T05:17:22Z WARN retrying request to api.private.redwood: connection reset by peer
```
I tried from my laptop: `curl -v https://api.private.redwood.company.net/v1/health` and it succeeds (shows proxy cert). But kube pods fail.

Mike: Two quick hypotheses: 1) Pod base image doesn't include the updated corporate MITM root CA in its OS-level truststore (common). 2) There's a transparent proxy that strips SNI and the server name reaching Redwood is wrong so mutual TLS or SNI-based routing fails.

Jordan: Can you run these on a failing pod and paste output?
```
# 1) curl with verbose to show cert
curl -vI https://api.private.redwood.company.net/v1/health
# 2) openssl to inspect handshake
openssl s_client -connect api.private.redwood.company.net:443 -servername api.private.redwood.company.net -showcerts
# 3) capture resolved IP
nslookup api.private.redwood.company.net || dig +short api.private.redwood.company.net
```

Sophia: Pasted outputs:
```
* Connected to 10.10.5.12 (10.10.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* unknown certificate authority
* Closing connection 0
```
Openssl shows the proxy presenting its MITM cert. Dig returns internal proxy IP 10.10.5.12.

Eva: Ok that confirms proxy MITM. Two things to check: a) whether the pod trust store includes the new corporate CA (Debian/Alpine/RHEL differences) and b) whether the private deployment expects TLS passthrough for certain endpoints. If your platform config expects passthrough but proxy terminates TLS and re-initiates to Redwood with a different SNI, the gateway may reject or route incorrectly.

Jordan: Also check conntrack / NAT table exhaustion errors on the proxy (we've seen proxies silently reset flows when conntrack is full leading to ECONNRESET on clients). Can you ask infra to check `conntrack -S` and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` around the timeframe?

Sophia: Infra checked: conntrack spikes were normal. However they confirmed the proxy CA bundle was rotated at 05:09 and our pod images are built 2 months ago (likely missing the new CA).

Mike: If pods are missing the CA, you have two quick mitigations: 1) inject the corporate root into pod truststore via initContainer that writes to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates && update-ca-certificates (Debian/Ubuntu), or 2) enable TLS passthrough for the egress node so proxy does SNI passthrough for api.private.redwood.company.net. Which is easier for you?

Sophia: Short term we'll patch images (initContainer) and redeploy. Longer term we'd prefer passthrough for Redwood endpoints. Is there any IP allowlist or cert pinning we should be aware of on Redwood Private side?

Jordan: For Private deployments we support both: if you configure network-level passthrough, Redwood sees original client cert/SNI. We don't require cert pinning by default, but customers often have egress allowlists (IP ranges) and SNI-based ACLs. If you switch to passthrough, ensure your firewall allows outbound to Redwood region CIDR and retains SNI. I'll DM you our published egress CIDR blocks and FQDNs.

Eva: Also note L4 passthrough removes MITM visibility so your security team will need exceptions. If you need to keep MITM, ensure you add the new corporate CA to all runtime images and system trust stores (and to language-specific stores, e.g., Java cacerts). For Java apps remember to run `keytool -importcert -trustcacerts -file corp.crt -keystore $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/cacerts` (password default change).

Sophia: Thanks — rolling a canary now with initContainer adding CA cert. Quick follow-up: some requests show 502 with body `upstream premature close` — could that be proxy reusing connections and failing on keepalive?

Mike: Yep, proxies occasionally close backend connections during MITM handshake mismatch or when idle connection pools mismatch TLS parameters. Check proxy logs for `upstream premature close` and increase keepalive/timeouts as a mitigation. Also ensure HTTP/2 is negotiated correctly; some MITM proxies don't handle HTTP/2 well and downgrade causing backend confusion.

Jordan: Filing ticket RN-12345 internally for tracking and I'll follow up with published egress CIDRs. incident-bot: created support case 12345 for Sophia. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: New support ticket #12345 created and linked to thread. Assigned to Jordan and Mike.

Sophia: Patch verified on canary pods — TLS errors gone, prod rollout in progress. Thanks for the quick help! :tada:
